messages:
Maria C: Heads up — saw a perf regression on long-seq inference after the last kernel-autotune pass. Ampere instances are picking a matmul path that looks slower for seqlen ~512. Any eyes on this?

Ashok P: Yep, saw p95 CPU/GPU time climb ~1.7x for batchable requests. Flamegraphs point to a fallback matmul kernel being selected by the runtime. :thinking:

Ben T: I ran a small bisect. When the runtime enables arch-aware kernel sets (selector v2) + dynamic seqlen routing we misclassify a chunk of traffic as "short" and end up using the smaller-kernel path which has bad perf at seqlen 512. The heuristic threshold is too aggressive.

Sarah L: Also noticed the KV cache keying: we only include model_id+version. If the kernel_profile changes, cached KV blobs persist and the runtime tries to reuse them -> mismatch and slower kernel fallback. We need the cache key to capture kernel_profile + seqlen_bucket + runtime_build.

Jun K: Important: we persist cached KV to RocksDB across restarts. If kernel ordering or serialization ABI changes, we must detect and skip old entries instead of blindly loading them. Suggested: include a small header with kv_version + runtime_build_hash in each blob.

perf-bot: Automated alert: p95 increased 1.7x for model "redwood-13b-quant" on region us-west-2. Flamegraph: https://perf.example/internal/fg/1775556789

Maria C: Proposed quick plan:
1) Change cache key to include kernel_profile_id and seqlen_bucket.
2) Add configurable TTL sweep and an API to trigger global invalidation when selector rollouts happen.
3) Add kv blob header with kv_version + runtime_build and skip incompatible blobs on load (log counts).

Ashok P: I'll own the TTL sweep + invalidation API. Will add endpoint: POST /v1/cache/invalidate with body {"reason":"kernel_profile_change","target":"all"}. Also add a cron mode for safety. :thumbsup:

Ben T: I'll update selector: compute a per-model seqlen_histogram during onboarding + live aggregation. Selector picks one of {short,medium,long} kernel paths based on percentile and has safe fallback rules when observed seqlen deviates. Add unit tests with synthetic seqlen distributions.

Sarah L: I'll draft a brief RFC for the new cache key format and migration strategy. Include a rollout plan: 1) add header and key change in runtime behind a feature flag, 2) gate full invalidation to control-plane toggle.

Jun K: Implementation detail for persistence: add a 4-byte magic + 1-byte kv_version + 32-byte runtime_build_hash prefix to each RocksDB value. On startup, scan and count skipped entries, expose metric `kv_persistence_skipped_total`.

Ben T: Quick example of proposed key + config: 
```
# proposed cache key example
model:redwood-13b:ver:2026-03-01:kernel_profile:kp-42:seqlen_bucket:long:kvsig:sha256(abcd1234)
```

```json
{
  "cache": {
    "key_format": "<model>:<ver>:<kernel_profile>:<seqlen_bucket>:<kvsig>",
    "persist": true,
    "ttl_seconds": 86400,
    "invalidate_triggers": ["kernel_profile_change","runtime_build_change","model_rollout"]
  }
}
```

Maria C: Nice. Action owners: @Ashok P (invalidate API + cron), @Ben T (selector + tests), @Sarah L (RFC + rollout), @Jun K (persistence header + metrics). Let's aim to land infra + runtime changes in next sprint and run an A/B on Ampere nodes.

Ashok P: I'll also add a small tooling script to trigger progressive invalidation per region to avoid thundering herd.

Sarah L: I'll include guidance in onboarding docs: seqlen histogram is required for private deployments so selector decisions are consistent.

Jun K: One more safety: write a migration that marks old blobs as tombstones (so we can backfill) instead of hard delete in case we need rollback.

Maria C: Great. If someone can drop a quick PR link when started, we'll triage. Thanks all. :rocket:
